renovation_cost_2026: Approximately $295 million (WFAA/StadiumDB reporting; ESPN reports a reported total close to $300 million). Covers the broader World Cup reconfiguration — raising/re-orienting the field and seating, natural-grass pitch system, and interior/facility upgrades — not the grass alone. Reported/estimated figure; exact audited total NOT SPECIFIED IN SOURCES.

renovations.change: Artificial turf replaced with a natural-grass pitch (Kentucky bluegrass + ryegrass blend) sod-grown in Colorado and installed by Precision Turf; supported by underground irrigation, ventilation/temperature control and retractable grow lights, to meet FIFA's natural-grass requirement.

iconic_games_note: AT&T Stadium has a genuine top-level football history as a repeat Concacaf Gold Cup and 2024 Copa América neutral host — the listed matches are individually sourced and verified. It is also a major non-football (American-football) venue: it hosted Super Bowl XLV (2011) and the College Football Playoff / Cotton Bowl, clearly labelled as non-soccer events and not counted as soccer lore.

city_history.founded: Arlington was incorporated in 1884; the metroplex anchor city of Dallas was founded in 1841.
city_history.significance: AT&T Stadium sits in Arlington, Texas, a city of roughly 390,000 between Dallas and Fort Worth that is the metroplex's sports/entertainment hub (also home to the Texas Rangers' Globe Life Field and Six Flags Over Texas). The Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex is one of the largest US metro areas (over 7 million people).
city_history.football_culture: Football (soccer) culture is hung on the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex rather than suburban Arlington: the metroplex hosts MLS side FC Dallas (Frisco), has a large and growing Hispanic/Latin American community driving strong support for Mexican and South American national teams, and AT&T Stadium has been a repeat neutral host for Concacaf Gold Cup and Copa América matches drawing large crowds.

sources.title: AT&T Stadium Dallas: 2026 World Cup Guide - Sofascore

stadium_history_facts: Opened May 27, 2009 as Cowboys Stadium; renamed AT&T Stadium in 2013 (naming-rights deal announced 25 July 2013).
Designed by HKS, Inc. at a construction cost of about $1.3 billion.
Home of the NFL's Dallas Cowboys; the largest NFL stadium by seating capacity (~80,000, reconfigurable past 100,000).
Features a retractable roof and one of the largest center-hung video boards in sports.
Hosted Super Bowl XLV (February 2011) and is a regular Concacaf Gold Cup and 2024 Copa América host venue.
For the 2026 World Cup it is FIFA-renamed 'Dallas Stadium' and converted to natural grass on a raised, widened pitch.
